item.title: Drogheda United to pay Dundalk pitch repairs
item.description: Drogheda United have confirmed they will pay the full cost of repairing Dundalk’s pitch after last week’s Louth derby. The League of Ireland had imposed a €15,000 fine on the club after last Friday’s game; where Drogheda fans threw flares onto the Oriel Park pitch. The incident was heavily condemned by minister for sport Patrick O’Donovan who was in attendance. item.title: Record high homelessness reported for last month
item.description: Over 17 thousand people are experiencing homelessness, the highest number ever recorded. Yesterday's figures include 5 thousand 300 children living in emergency accommodation, a 15.6 percent increase since January 2025. The report shows the number of people accessing emergency accommodation has also gone up by 12 per cent over the last 12 months, while the number of homeless families has risen by more than 18 per cent. item.title: Average cost of three-bed home in Cavan rises to over €1,400
item.description: A three-bedroom house costs an average of €1,467 to rent in Co. Cavan. That's according to the latest Daft.ie figures for Q4 of 2025. Figures show that during that period, prices for a three-bedroom house in the Breffni county rose by 5.6%. Four-bedroom houses also rose to €1,652 on average, while rents for a one bedroom apartment rose by 11.1%. item.title: Over 30 Cavan homeowners benefit from First Home Scheme
item.description: 31 homeowners in Cavan have benefitted from the First Home Scheme. The scheme has supported 5,000 home purchases nationally, since its launch in 2022. Under the initiative funding is offered to first-time buyers who, despite having a deposit and mortgage approval in place, still could not cover the cost of a new-build home. item.title: Children with special needs 'easy targets' in budget cuts - Monaghan mother
item.description: A Co Monaghan mother and campaigner says children with special needs are "easy targets" when it comes to Government spending. According to Oliva Larkin, the coalition is behind on 200 classrooms for children with special education and is not willing to fund them. item.title: Lavin claims eighth national title
item.description: Sarah Lavin (Emerald AC) claimed her eighth national indoor 60m hurdles title at the national indoor championships today. Lavin powered past of World silver heptathlon medallist Kate O’Connor (Dundalk St Gerards) who set a huge indoor personal best on her season opener.
